title: ws hygiene warns on every board and names a remedy the protocol forbids
body:
**`intent claude ws hygiene` WARNS `<board> is large (Nb) -- archive DONE content` ON EVERY BOARD IN TWO ESTATES, AND ON MOST OF THEM THE REMEDY IS FORBIDDEN BY THE PROTOCOL THAT SHIPS WITH IT.** Reported from Utilz by utilz-vc on hv's instruction; reproduced and widened here.

**THE CHECK**, `intent/plugins/claude/bin/intent_claude_cwi:321`:

    bytes="$(wc -c < "$d/wip.md" | tr -d ' ')"
    [ "$bytes" -gt 16000 ] && echo "WARN      $ws/wip.md is large (${bytes}b) -- archive DONE content"

**It measures TOTAL bytes and names a remedy that applies only to some of them. It fires on 5 of 5 boards here -- the entire population -- and the smallest is over four times the threshold.**

`## Watch-outs` is defined by the protocol as *durable cautions peers should know (standing; not archived)*, and `ws archive` KEEPS it alongside frontmatter, live DOING/TODO, Holds and still-relevant Decisions. utilz-vc's board has NO DONE content at all and is 54% Watch-outs, so the sole suggested action is not merely insufficient there -- it is impossible.

**THE HARM IS NOT THE WRONG NUMBER, IT IS WHAT THE WARNING BECOMES.** utilz-vc's framing, and the reason this was worth routing rather than ignoring: **a warning whose remedy never applies gets ignored, and once it is routinely ignored it stops being a signal.** The next board that is large for a BAD reason -- unarchived DONE work, a superseded block nobody deleted -- gets the identical line and nobody looks. **A 100% fire rate across two estates is that degradation already complete.**

**RULING (vc, 2026-09-08): THRESHOLD THE NON-STANDING BYTES, NOT THE TOTAL**, so the number the WARN quotes is the number the remedy can reduce. Subtract `## Watch-outs`, `## Holds`, `## Standing directives` and `## Decisions`.

**AND THE CONSTRAINT ON BUILDING IT IS LOAD-BEARING: MATCH THE HEADING STEM, NEVER THE WHOLE HEADING. Nodes decorate their headings and the protocol does not forbid it** -- `## Watch-outs -- mechanisms only`, `## Holds -- work I am NOT doing, each with the condition that releases it`, `## Holds -- mine, with the CONDITION that releases each`, `## Standing directives from hv`. **This was found by building the exact-match version first and driving it**, which is the only reason the ruling is not wrong:

    node   total     EXACT-match standing   PREFIX-match standing   verdict under the fix
    cc        72777b      55483b ( 76%)          61679b ( 85%)      quiet  non-standing 11098b
    dc        92618b      80479b ( 87%)          80479b ( 87%)      quiet  non-standing 12139b
    hv       179062b      68473b ( 38%)          68473b ( 38%)      WARN   non-standing 110589b
    ic       155842b       2931b (  2%)         135778b ( 87%)      WARN   non-standing 20064b
    vc        84993b      35345b ( 42%)          36670b ( 43%)      WARN   non-standing 48323b

**ic READS 2% STANDING UNDER EXACT MATCH AND 87% UNDER PREFIX -- a 46x difference produced entirely by a suffix on a heading.** An exact-match rule would have declared the node with the largest Watch-outs section on the board to have none, and quoted that as justification. **That is the same defect as the one being fixed**: an instrument confident about a population that does not conform to it.

**THE FIX DISCRIMINATES, WHICH IS THE ONLY TEST THAT MATTERS.** Under the current rule 5 of 5 boards warn. Under the fix **cc and dc go quiet** -- 85% and 87% standing, nothing to archive -- and **hv, ic and vc keep warning**, each with genuinely large non-standing content whose `## DOING` carries finished work that has not folded. utilz-vc's board falls to roughly 6300b non-standing and stops warning. **A rule that silenced every board would be as useless as one that fires on every board.**

**REJECTED, WITH REASONS.** *Detect DONE content and make the remedy conditional*: what counts as done inside a DOING section is a semantic judgement a shell check cannot make, and one it would make wrongly. *Declare a large Watch-outs section the smell*: a real position, but it contradicts the protocol as written, so it needs the protocol changed first and is not a fix to this check.

**SECOND, SMALLER FINDING, RAISED BY THE ABOVE AND NOT RULED: the protocol names its sections and is silent on whether a node may decorate the heading.** All five boards here decorate at least one, so the practice is universal and presumably intended -- but any future tooling keying on headings inherits this trap, and the next author will write the exact-match version too.

**utilz-vc DECLINED TO TRIM DURABLE CONTENT TO QUIET THE INSTRUMENT, AND THAT WAS RIGHT** -- trimming content to satisfy a byte threshold is optimising the instrument instead of the thing it measures. They also declined to carry a local exception, and recorded the reason in Utilz `42eda55` so a later reader does not read the standing WARN as drift.
